scope: full benchmark suite verification: complex codec, Track B, criterion function_dispatch; single machine, fresh measurements on current checkout

environment.machine: Apple M1 Max (T6000, arm64), 8P+2E cores, 64 GiB RAM
environment.criterionMode: Baseline::Save (default): fresh run -> new/, copied to base/; change/ only when base/ pre-existed
environment.envSanitization: all bun/cargo invocations ran under env -u RUSTRA_BUN_LIBRARY (loop-daemon dylib contamination)

limitations: does not measure Rust or C++ native dispatch
does not measure Rust handler or C++ JSI marshalling (device smoke required)
three wall-clock executions in one process, per-op median reported
measures the JS codec path only — the C++ direct path is native and not measurable from this script

functionDispatch.command: env -u RUSTRA_BUN_LIBRARY cargo bench -p rustra --bench function_dispatch

baseline.source: target/criterion/function_dispatch/<bench>/pre-perf/estimates.json (snapshot 2026-09-18; identical values to the pre-run new/ that this run overwrote)
baseline.receipt2026_09_22: docs/benchmark-receipts/2026-09-22-function-dispatch-smoke.json (different bench binary; legacy_json median 441.49 ns -> -38.1% vs fresh)

conclusions: No regressions: all six criterion benches improved 3.2-21.3% vs the pre-perf baseline; deltas are within the repo regression-gate thresholds (maxRegression 0.10, maxImprovement 0.35, no mixed improvement/regression pattern).

Baseline provenance caveat: the pre-perf baseline's compiler cannot be verified from stored data (docs/benchmarks.md cites Rust 1.98.0 for the 2026-09-16 patch measurements while this run used the pinned 1.95.0); part of the uniform improvement may be toolchain/codegen difference rather than source change.

function vs legacy dispatch is now equivalent on frame/into paths (37.5 ns / 14.8 ns both) — tuple-input functions no longer pay a dispatch penalty; json path remains ~7x slower for legacy structs (HashMap-based deserialization of named fields).

JS codec path costs are microsecond-scale (0.46-3.53 us/op), i.e. 3-4 orders of magnitude above the native frame dispatch floor (~15-40 ns), consistent with the documented motivation for C++ direct marshalling on Track B.
All numbers are single-machine single-process measurements; a CI baseline is required before using them as regression gates (agreed with rust-tests and ts-tests dependency conclusions).
